chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said:

One day I performed wudu (ablution) and did not wash my private part, then I performed salat (prayer). So I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: Wash your private part and repeat your salat (prayer).
Thus he made obligatory the repetition of the salat (prayer) and the washing of the place, according to what we have explained in detail.

key_terms.أَغْسِلْ: to wash in the sense of removing impurity here
key_terms.غَسْلَ: washing as an obligatory act of purification
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer that must be repeated here
key_terms.ٱلْمَوْضِعِ: the affected place or area to be washed

ai.seo_question: If someone performs salat (prayer) without washing the private part properly, must the prayer be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning taharah (ritual purity) in relation to salat (prayer). It indicates that if one prayed after failing to wash the private part, one must wash the affected place and repeat the salat (prayer).
